bullets.title: NVDA/Semis: DeepSeek developing own AI chip; broad chip complex sells off 3-6%
bullets.body: Reuters reported DeepSeek is developing its own inference-stage AI chip to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei, sending NVDA down ~1.7% premarket. The broader semiconductor complex sold off sharply: MU -4.7%, MRVL -4.6%, AMD -3.7%, SNDK -4.4%, STX -5.0%, WDC -6.1%, INTC -4%. GS TMT notes the SOX is up 88% YTD vs S&P +14%, creating less favorable risk/reward despite estimate upside; JPM maintains tactical bullish view, calling the semis pullback a buying opportunity given Mag7 at 10-year valuation lows vs SPX.

bullets.title: AVGO: Erste Group downgrades to hold from buy
bullets.body: Erste Group downgraded Broadcom to hold from buy Tuesday morning, adding to pressure on the stock which is down ~2.2% premarket. AVGO represents ~39% of NDX alongside Mag7 per JPM, elevating rotation risk given stretched semis valuations.

bullets.title: NET: Scotiabank upgrades to sector outperform, PT $300 from $225
bullets.body: Scotiabank GBM upgraded Cloudflare to sector outperform from sector perform and raised its price target to $300 from $225, implying ~21% upside from $247.55. NET is up 3.4% premarket, outperforming as software/cloud names benefit from the AI sovereignty/DeepSeek narrative (inference demand remains intact even as chip supply diversifies).

bullets.title: META: Erste upgrades to buy; four states seek $1.4T in penalties over youth safety
bullets.body: Erste Group upgraded Meta to buy from hold. Offsetting the positive, four US states are seeking $1.4T in penalties at an August trial over addictive design and youth safety claims; Meta calls the figure unprecedented and unsupported. Stock is up only ~0.3% premarket, suggesting the market is discounting the penalty risk as unlikely to be realized at headline size.

bullets.title: AAPL: JPM raises PT to $345, FY27 EPS ~$9.85 on price elasticity resilience
bullets.body: JPM updated AAPL estimates to reflect ~20% market-wide hardware price increases, forecasting a $100 iPhone 18 ASP increase (vs. $50 prior) with only a -7% volume decline in FY27—less bad than feared. FY27 EPS held at ~$9.85; Dec-27 PT raised to $345 at 32x CY28 earnings. Historical data shows iPhone unit share actually rose from 15% to 19-20% despite ~50% ASP increases over FY15-FY26.

bullets.title: AVGO/AAPL: Broadcom extends Apple partnership through 2031 for custom chips
bullets.body: Broadcom extended its custom chip development and supply partnership with Apple through 2031; Apple represents ~20% of Broadcom revenue. The extension provides revenue visibility for AVGO's HPC/custom silicon segment even amid broader semi weakness.

bullets.title: TXN: Citi sees best analog semi positioning; models Q3 sales +7.5% Q/Q vs consensus +7%
bullets.body: Citi calls TXN best-positioned in analog semis given improving global PMI (May 52.6, strongest in 3 years), ~85% internal manufacturing capacity, pricing power, and data center share gains in H2. Citi models Q3 GM at 60.5% vs consensus 60.2% and 2027 EPS of $10.10 vs consensus $9.20. MPWR flagged as cautious given potential Stage 2 power share loss to TXN in H2.

bullets.title: TSM: JPM raises PT to NT$3,100 on AI demand; FY26/27/28E EPS +5/10/16%
bullets.body: JPM raised its TSMC Jun-27 price target to NT$3,100 (20x 12-month forward earnings) from NT$2,925, lifting FY26/27/28E EPS by 5%/10%/16%. Near-term gross margins expected to nudge toward 70%; TSMC seen pushing back on share loss concerns and expanding capacity meaningfully in 2027-29. Datacenter AI CAGR now estimated at 69% from 2024-29E; broader price hikes expected in 2027 given supply-demand gap.

bullets.title: GLW: Oppenheimer raises PT to $230 on BOE AI partnership; views selloff as entry
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raised Corning's price target to $230 from $215 (Outperform) after BOE highlighted Corning as a key partner for AI chip packaging, optical interconnects, foldable displays, and solar. Shares are ~27% below June highs; the firm views the AI infrastructure selloff as an attractive entry point.

bullets.title: MRVL: Non-deal roadshows in Edinburgh and Zurich/Geneva July 7-8
bullets.body: Marvell Technology is hosting non-deal roadshows in Edinburgh (July 7) and Zurich/Geneva (July 8), a potential signal of upcoming investor outreach ahead of earnings season. Stock is down ~4-5% premarket alongside the broader chip complex.

bullets.title: MSFT: Xbox restructuring with 3,200 layoffs; operating at 3-10x below platform peer margins
bullets.body: Microsoft is restructuring Xbox with 3,200 layoffs over FY27, including 1,600 immediate cuts and four studios leaving the division. Xbox currently operates at 3-10x lower margins than comparable platform/publishing businesses. Additionally, MDB CEO discussed Claude Code recommending Voyage AI embeddings, and Wolfe flagged MSFT as conducting broader layoffs.

bullets.title: PLTR: Up 1.5% on GNP Seguros enterprise expansion agreement
bullets.body: Palantir is up 1.5% premarket after announcing an enterprise expansion agreement with GNP Seguros. Separately, Zeta Global is rearchitecting its Data Cloud onto Palantir Foundry with a mid-August go-live target, with at least one joint enterprise customer expected to launch—a positive incremental demand signal for PLTR's AIP platform.

bullets.title: NOW/Software cloud: Outperforming on DeepSeek inference demand thesis; Jefferies cautious on app software
bullets.body: NOW is up 2.8% premarket alongside NET as the market interprets DeepSeek's chip development (reducing training-chip reliance on NVDA) as bullish for inference/software spend. However, Jefferies maintains underweight on application software, citing AI budgets crowding out core software spend, frontier lab threats to software moats, and seat-based licensing under pressure; favors infra/security over app software.

bullets.title: FSLR: Deutsche Bank upgrades to buy; stock +3.6% premarket
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank upgraded First Solar to buy from hold, sending shares up 3.6% in premarket trading. No specific price target was disclosed in the items received.

bullets.title: HOOD: Mizuho maintains $130 PT; Jefferies flags as top broker/wealth idea
bullets.body: Mizuho updated HOOD FY26E revenue to ~$4.98bn and FY27E to ~$6.12bn, holding its $130 PT at ~18x FY27E revenue and calling it a credible first global brokerage hyperscaler candidate. Separately, Jefferies cited HOOD as its favorite idea in the US broker/wealth 2Q26 preview, noting positive EPS estimate revisions (+2% avg for 2Q26) driven by higher trading activity and margin balances. Stock also rallying on the Trump accounts introduction theme.

bullets.title: CMCSA/CHTR: Morgan Stanley cuts PTs, models cable broadband subs declining 3-4% CAGR through 2030
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cut CMCSA PT to $30 and T to $25 on Starlink broadband threat, forecasting ~16mn Starlink subs by 2030 (11% US household penetration) and cable broadband sub losses at 3-4% CAGR. MS AlphaWise survey shows cable satisfaction lowest at 46% vs FWA at 63%; over 30% of broadband subs likely to switch ISPs in next 12 months. TMUS remains top pick as fastest wireless growth with least legacy exposure.

bullets.title: EQIX: Remains most crowded long in REIT universe per UBS quant; DLR moved to net short
bullets.body: UBS quant data shows REIT average crowding score fell from 4.9 in May to 3.9 in June. EQIX remains among the most crowded longs with a stable score. DLR experienced a notable score decrease in June and moved to a solid net short position—a meaningful positioning shift worth monitoring ahead of 2Q earnings.

bullets.title: VRT/CRNX: Vertex acquiring Crinetics for $85/sh (~$10B); adds >$5B peak-sales endocrine pillar
bullets.body: Vertex is acquiring Crinetics Pharmaceuticals at $85/share cash (~100% premium, ~$10B equity value), expected to close 3Q26. Palsonify (FDA/EMA-approved acromegaly oral therapy) and atumelnant (Phase 3 CAH candidate) add a >$5B peak-sales endocrine franchise. Citi maintains Buy on VRTX at $585 PT; non-GAAP operating income accretion expected 2029.

bullets.title: NVDA Blackwell cloud ramp: +11% m/m to 254 instances per KeyBanc tracker
bullets.body: KeyBanc's June cloud instance tracker shows NVDA Blackwell instances up 11% m/m to 254 with three new Grace Blackwell instances (6 total). Total cloud instances +1% m/m, +14% y/y. AMD Turin +5% m/m; INTC Granite Rapids +7% m/m. Accelerator growth returned to positive (+1% m/m) after -2% m/m in May—supportive of near-term GPU demand despite DeepSeek chip headline.

bullets.title: WULF/SEI/GEV/CEG: Power infrastructure commentary; WULF deal at ~22% implied yield topped expectations
bullets.body: MS energy feedback: WULF deal terms exceeded expectations with ~22% implied yield vs HUT's 18.6% and 17% buyside expectations. SEI's GESA acquisition to diversify into EPC viewed constructively. ERCOT Batch Zero approval expected mid-August, potentially unlocking incremental IPP contracting demand for VST/CEG. MS maintains OW on power names (CEG, TLN, VST), power equipment (BE, GEV), and power solutions (SEI), citing Meta neocloud news as validating compute demand math.
